title: Fixed Leading Edge Access Panel — Removal

ata.title: Wing Leading Edge — Fixed Leading Edge Structure

abstract: Removal of a fixed leading edge access panel with the slat support that must be in place first, and the hole condition record that decides whether the panel can be refitted as it is.

sections.purpose: This task removes an access panel from the fixed leading edge so that the structure, the harnesses or the anti-ice ducting behind it can be reached, and records the fastener hole condition at every position.
sections.job_setup_note: Nobody works under a slat that is not supported. The panel is large and light and will be taken by the wind; do not remove it in a gust above the limit in the maintenance manual. Record the hole condition as you go rather than at the end, because an elongated hole is much easier to see with the fastener just removed than after all of them are out.
sections.procedure: 1. Extend the slats to the position given in the maintenance manual and fit the slat supports. WARNING: DO NOT WORK UNDER AN UNSUPPORTED SLAT. THE SYSTEM CAN RETRACT ON RESIDUAL HYDRAULIC PRESSURE. 2. Check the wind against the limit before the panel is released. 3. Position the panel support trestle under the panel in zone 512 or zone 613 as applicable. 4. Release the fasteners in the sequence marked on the panel, working from the centre outwards. CAUTION: RELEASE THE FASTENERS FROM THE CENTRE OUTWARDS. WORKING FROM ONE END PUTS THE WHOLE PANEL LOAD ONTO THE LAST FEW FASTENERS AND ELONGATES THEIR HOLES. 5. As each fastener is removed, look at its hole and record any elongation, any missing anchor nut and any sign of the anchor nut turning. 6. Support the panel and lower it onto the trestle. 7. Examine the panel land and the moulded seal, where fitted, for damage and for water tracking. 8. Where the seal is a sealant bead, examine the drain hole and record whether it is open. 9. Examine the rib flange behind the panel for corrosion and record the extent. 10. Examine the doubler OR583107-28 at the forward edge, where fitted, for disbond at the edges. 11. Check the microswitch 3VU2 and its harness for security. 12. Check the edging grommet EN301916-66 at the harness pass-through. 13. Cover the aperture if the panel will be off for more than one shift.
sections.close_out: Record the hole condition at every fastener position on the panel map, the rib flange condition and the drain hole state. Do not refit a panel with more than the number of elongated holes given in the limits table; refer it to engineering.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft; step 8 applies only to panels with the sealant bead rather than the moulded seal

safety_precautions: Fit the slat supports before working under the leading edge.
Check the wind limit before releasing the panel.
Two people are needed to lower the panel.
